worked_solution:
First, we divide both the numerator and the denominator by the highest power of $x$ in the denominator, which is ${x}^{2}.$ Then, by noting that the reciprocals shrink to $0$ in the limit, we can then evaluate the resulting expression.

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{3-x-8{x}^{2}}{k\,{x}^{2}+7x-4} & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{(\frac{3}{{x}^{2}}-\frac{x}{{x}^{2}}-\frac{8{x}^{2}}{{x}^{2}})}{(\frac{k{x}^{2}}{\,{x}^{2}}+\frac{7x}{{x}^{2}}-\frac{4}{{x}^{2}})} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{(\frac{3}{{x}^{2}}-\frac{1}{x}-8)}{(k+\frac{7}{x}-\frac{4}{{x}^{2}})} \\  & =\frac{0-0-8}{k+0-0} \\  & =\frac{-8}{k} \\  & =-\frac{8}{k}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}-\frac{8}{k} & =\frac{2}{5} \\ 2k & =-40 \\ k & =-20.\end{aligned}
$$
